stage_a.note: F1 enters with a big smile, waving enthusiastically, and maintains an upbeat tone.
High energy delivery, especially when F2 dramatically smashes the bag of ice.
Friendly and approachable demeanor, though mostly focused on delivering the pitch points.

venture.description: A portable beverage cooler with built-in freezing gel that eliminates the need for ice.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces himself and the company, then presents the Chiller as a portable beverage cooler with freezing gel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 enters carrying a bag of ice and apologizes for being late.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that the Chiller does not require ice to keep drinks cold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 complains about the inconvenience of buying ice and dramatically smashes the bag of ice on the floor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he put the Chiller in the freezer overnight and loaded it with drinks.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 states that the drinks will stay cold for a while.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shows that the cooler can hold many types of cans and large bottles like champagne.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms the cooler can hold large bottles.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 points out the compact size of the cooler.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 agrees and notes that the cooler is also heavy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 claims the Chiller is the future of portable cooling, saving time, money, and the environment.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 reacts to the mess of the smashed ice on the floor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 highlights their sustainable solution, reducing water waste and single-use plastics, and their donation to clean water projects.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 invites the panel to partner with them, asking for 150k for 15 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 handles the product, demonstrating that it can hold cans or bottles by removing the cans.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees with S4 that the product is incredibly versatile.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 questions the cooler's capacity, noting it only holds three cans, which he would finish quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies that they have heard that feedback from macho men on the internet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 adds that people often complain about the three-beer capacity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how he is supposed to take a whole case of beer with him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that users can swap a cold can out and put a new one in to chill.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how long the cooler keeps beverages cold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that it stays cold for six hours.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks the founders what their sales have been.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 answers they have done 111k in sales to date, starting with a Kickstarter campaign.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what the product costs to make.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 admits that their product cost is currently awful.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 repeats the word awful in reaction to the founder's admission.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 advises the founder never to start an answer by calling their cost awful.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains that their first run cost 18 dollars a unit to build, plus importing costs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 calculates that the cost is up to 22 dollars with the added sleeves.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms the sleeves added another 11 dollars to the cost.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 calculates that the total cost is now up to 32 dollars.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms the cost went all the way up to 37 dollars for the initial units.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses shock that the product costs 37 dollars to make.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 clarifies that was only for the first run and they have since brought the cost down to 18 dollars.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they are currently selling the initial expensive units at a loss to prove the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that this is the first sustainable portable beverage chiller.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 challenges the claim that the product is the only sustainable cooler on the market.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 questions the sustainability, pointing out the large amount of plastic used in the cooler's construction.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues the product is built to last forever and that all materials are recyclable.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 points out that the plastic bags they are replacing are also recyclable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters that only a small percentage of thrown-away plastic is actually recycled.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks the founders why they decided to enter the cooler market given their backgrounds.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they had good jobs at Google and Apple but decided to build this business on the side.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what roles the founders held at Google and Apple.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that he worked in sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 answers that he worked in finance.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the founders are still working at their corporate jobs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 answers that they quit their jobs two years ago to do this full-time.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the founders are making enough money to sustain themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that they are not yet making money.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 adds that they have not taken a salary since leaving their jobs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokingly asks if they want him to make a call to get their old jobs back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 politely declines, stating they are very happy doing what they are doing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains their mission is to address the massive amount of plastic waste.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 challenges their decision to leave promising careers, comparing it to sailors being lured to crash on the rocks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks the founders who their number one competitor is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that their main competitor is ice.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 repeats ice in a questioning tone, seeking confirmation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokes about going to anger management therapy to be a nicer investor this season.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 questions the valuation, asking if they are out of their minds to ask for 150k for 15 percent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 responds that they are not out of their minds regarding the valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 challenges the business idea, calling the product a tchotchke that beer companies give away.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends the product, stating it is sustainable and convenient.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses deep frustration, stating he wants to rip the founders to pieces.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 tells the founders to stop, calling the business a really bad idea with no hope.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks again why they chose to make coolers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 states he does not buy the sustainability angle, hates the product, and decides to exit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 criticizes the founders' presentation, advising them to stick to their features next time they pitch.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 acknowledges the product works but exits due to the poor presentation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 calls the other investors clinically insane if they give the founders a reason to continue.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 advises that the product must be the protagonist and the social mission cannot be a crutch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues that the social mission is not a crutch but their core mission.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they could have been wealthy in their corporate jobs but wanted to make a difference.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 challenges F2, stating that his reasoning does not make any sense.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 clarifies they also wanted to learn, feeling they were not learning enough at Apple and Google.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 challenges the founders' credibility, criticizing their claim that ice is their main competitor.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 criticizes their pivoting story, noting the product is made of plastic and their motivations keep changing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 reiterates that he simply was not learning enough at his previous job.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 concludes that it was a bad presentation overall and decides to exit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 advises the founders that it is crucial to get their manufacturing costs down to make it affordable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states the product is not what she is interested in investing in and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states he is not confident it is a huge business but believes they will figure it out, exiting.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 congratulates the founders on what they have accomplished so far.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 wishes the founders good luck as they leave the tank.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 defends his positive comments to the other investors, stating he thinks it is a good-looking product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokingly asks S3 how long his anger management classes were.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 plays along, claiming he listened and has been great.

decisions.note: Hates the sustainability angle, doesn't buy it, thinks it's a tchotchke.
Thinks the presentation was terrible and they didn't sell it well.
Story has lapses in credibility, too many pivots, bad presentation.
Needs to get cost down, not the type of product she wants to invest in.
Not confident it's a huge business, though he believes the founders will figure things out eventually.
